author: @FrankCurzio
text:
Elon just admitted Grok costs more to run than it brings in.

Which raises the question...

If AI loses this much money, why is everyone still pouring trillions into it?

After my post on Saturday, someone asked me exactly that. Fair question, but there's a good reason every company is still doing it:

Losing money early isn't new.

Amazon didn't post a full-year profit until 2003, nine years after it started. Everyone called it a joke. I remember being on Wall Street watching it happen.

And it's a similar story now with AI.

The giants spending the most on AI aren't doing it for the chatbot. AI runs on their clouds, and cloud is one of the most profitable businesses on earth. Amazon's runs at margins near 40%. Every company that wants AI has to rent it from them.

More importantly, nobody wants to be the one who sat this out either.

Whoever owns the AI infrastructure for the next 20 years wins, so they'd rather overspend now than lose the whole damn thing.

And it gets cheaper. Every technology starts out expensive and clunky. The cost of running these models keeps falling, and whoever builds the infrastructure now makes the money when it does.

Does that mean everyone wins? Hell no.

The guys who borrowed billions with no real customers are going to get crushed, and some won't make it. And the companies that fired half their staff thinking AI could run itself are already learning that the hard way.

Look at Elon's own numbers. Grok loses money, but every dollar it burns goes to someone: the chips, the power, the data centers. And that's the best part.

Some will think that's fucking absurd, because a lot of these stocks have been annihilated in recent weeks.

CoreWeave is down over 70% from its high. Vertiv is down about half... BUT the money is still flowing to them.

Vertiv’s orders more than doubled last quarter, and CoreWeave has over $100B of signed business. What got crushed was the price, because the market panicked about who’s going to pay for all of this.

And the spending isn't slowing down. I think we hit $7T on AI infrastructure by 2030.

Will there be pain along the way?

Absolutely.

These stocks will keep swinging 10 to 15% at a time, and you have to be OK with that. But this is the biggest spending cycle I've seen in 30 years on Wall Street, and it's still early.

Be careful out there, but don't sit this one out.

author: @FrankCurzio
text:
JUST IN: China just bought more foreign oil than in any month since March.

Imports hit 9.88 million barrels a day in October, up 9.4% from September, because tankers from the Persian Gulf are finally moving again after this year's Iran war.

Don't read this as a boom.

China drained its own tanks during the war. In September its stockpiles fell faster than ever recorded. A lot of this buying is just refilling them.

And imports are still 13% below a year ago.

Brent fell 3.6% to $94 on hopes of a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. This week Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was attacked & a tanker caught fire near the Strait. I'm not treating $94 as the all-clear.

I'm watching CF Industries $CF closely. Fertilizer makers won when Hormuz closed. That trade reverses as Gulf shipping returns.

The war burned through the world's spare oil, and even with a deal, rebuilding that cushion takes months.

Oil's floor is HIGHER now than it was before the war.
media_note: 中国原油輸入量の棒グラフ。2025年10月から2026年10月まで、10月は9.9百万バレル/日を強調。
